about: Where the weekly money could go, for Mint's Plan tab. One entry per path; adding a path is one entry here. kind cash: a savings account on the RBA cash rate. kind fund: a mix of the assets below, minus fees and tax. kind zero_skill: a CFD trader who picks directions by coin flip, run by the Lab on real prices with every real cost. Futures for cash and fund paths are built from 12-month runs of real months since history.first_month, the same months for every path in a future, so they share the same luck. A dividend income comes from symbols.json (dividend_yield_pct). Figures come from docs/library/money/2026-10-09-research-*.md; 'assumption' marks a reasoned guess.

au.label: Australian shares: S&P/ASX 200 plus dividends
au.income_tax_note: Dividends of 4.0% a year, about 75% franked: tax at 32% on the grossed-up amount less the franking credit is about 0.4% of the balance a year (computed).

us.label: US shares: S&P 500 plus dividends, in Australian dollars
us.income_tax_note: Dividends of 1.5% a year taxed at 32% (the 15% US withholding counts towards it): about 0.48% of the balance a year (computed).

tax.note: On a salary between $45,001 and $135,000: 30% tax plus 2% Medicare levy on the next dollar; half of a gain held over a year is taxed, so 16% of it, and a gain on money held under a year is taxed in full; dividends kept in a fund were taxed the year they came and count in the cost base, so selling does not tax them again; super contributions taxed 15%; the $32,500 concessional cap counts the employer's 12% Super Guarantee too, so salary sacrifice can add $32,500 less 12% of the salary (ATO).

comfort.label: A 15% fall would keep me up at night
I can sit through a 30% fall
I can watch half of it vanish for a while, as in 2008

paths.label: High-interest savings account
paths.summary: A bank account paying about the cash rate plus a little: 5.00% today at Macquarie with no conditions. Guaranteed by the government up to $250,000 per person per bank. The interest is taxed at your rate every year, so 5.00% keeps about 3.4%.
sources: RBA cash rate 4.60% from 30 Sep 2026 (RBA table A2)
Financial Claims Scheme: $250,000 per person per bank (APRA)
assumptions: The bank paid 0.4 points over the cash rate in every past month (today's gap; an assumption).

paths.label: Australian shares index fund (VAS or A200)
paths.summary: One ETF holding the 200 to 300 biggest Australian companies, bought once a month. Fees 0.07% a year plus $3 a buy. Dividends are taxed each year (franking credits cover most of it), and 16% of the gain when you sell after a year.
sources: S&P/ASX 200 prices from Yahoo; dividends 4.0% a year measured from VAS.AX and STW.AX

paths.label: All-growth shares fund, Australia and the world (DHHF)
paths.summary: One ETF holding thousands of companies, roughly 40% Australian and 60% overseas, bought once a month. Fees 0.19% a year plus $3 a buy. The overseas part rises and falls with the dollar.
sources: Overseas part modelled with the S&P 500 in Australian dollars (AUD/USD from Yahoo; CME Australian dollar futures before May 2006)
assumptions: The S&P 500 stands in for world shares: the US is most of a world index but not all of it, so a real world fund will differ.

paths.label: Extra super by salary sacrifice (growth option)
paths.summary: Your employer pays part of your salary into super before tax. Giving up $300 of take-home pay puts about $375 into super, because super contributions are taxed 15% instead of a typical 32%. The catch: it is locked until you are 60.
paths.locked: Locked until 60. Up to $50,000 of voluntary contributions can come out early for a first home through the First Home Super Saver scheme.
sources: First Home Super Saver: $15,000 a year, $50,000 in total (ATO)
assumptions: Fund fees 0.6% a year (typical growth option; an assumption).
Tax inside super on earnings about 0.7% of the balance a year after franking credits (an assumption).

paths.label: Trading ASX 200 CFDs with no real edge
paths.summary: A Plus500-style account trading the ASX 200 at 5x leverage, about 25 trades a year held 5 days, each direction picked by a coin flip, paying a Plus500-style spread and overnight funding (the ASX 200 spread and the 3% funding markup are assumptions: Plus500's own figures could not be read). This is what trading looks like until someone proves an edge. ASIC found 68% of Australian retail CFD clients lost money in FY24.
sources: ASIC REP 828: 68% of retail CFD clients lost money in FY24

Costs from published broker fees: no commission, the 0.7% conversion fee and nightly funding are Plus500's published terms; the ASX 200 spread (0.02%) and the 3% markup over the cash rate are assumptions
assumptions: Profit is taxed as income at 32%; losses are not used against other income here.
Runs at most 10 years: a trading account is a quick-income track, and longer windows of real history repeat too much.

info.label: Pay off a HECS-HELP debt early?
lines: A HECS debt grows with indexation: 2.8% for 2026. Paying it early is a sure 2.8% a year, tax-free.
Each dollar of income over $69,528 repays 15 cents. Just over that line the yearly repayment can be smaller than a year's indexation, so a debt can barely shrink on its own.
Savings at 5.00% keep about 3.4% after tax, so paying early is roughly a draw with savings and worse than shares over the long run. It does end the 15 cents a dollar on income over $69,528.
sources: ATO HELP indexation 2.8% (2026) and repayment thresholds

info.label: Side income Claude can help build
lines: Local clients (small-business sites, booking forms, Python automations): $0 to $8,000 in year one, 5 to 8 hours a week. The hard part is finding clients, not building.
Freelance platforms (Upwork, Fiverr): $0 to $5,000, 5 to 10 hours a week, much of it unpaid bidding at first.
A paid niche tool or template (Gumroad, itch.io): $0 to $2,000. About half of listed indie products earn nothing.
sources: Mint's research notes on side income (the ranking; year-one figures are judgement)
